statement: Self-limiting ALD of Mo from MoCl2O2 and atomic hydrogen occurs between 150 and 450 °C.
definition_note: Self-limiting ALD growth window spans 150 to 450 °C.

statement: Atomic hydrogen is necessary to reduce MoCl2O2 since molecular H2 yields no deposition.
definition_note: Atomic hydrogen is required for MoCl2O2 reduction.

statement: Films deposited at or above 350 °C contain about 95 at.% Mo.
Films deposited at or above 350 °C contain about 3.5 at.% oxygen.
The growth per cycle in the plateau regime is around 0.022 nm/cycle.
Film resistivity reaches 18.6 µΩ·cm at 24 nm thickness.
Oxygen impurity levels increase up to 33 at.% when the deposition temperature decreases to 150 °C.
definition_note: Decreasing temperature raises oxygen incorporation.

statement: Chlorine levels reach 2.7 at.% at 150 °C.
definition_note: Chlorine incorporation increases at lower temperature.

statement: Low resistivity metallic Mo films require deposition temperatures of 250 °C or higher.
definition_note: Lower temperatures increase resistivity and impurity levels.

statement: Prior Mo-oxychloride reduction using molecular hydrogen was conducted between 450 and 590 °C.
Thermal ALD using MoCl2O2 and H2 was previously performed at 600 to 650 °C.
Atomic hydrogen enables reduction of MoCl2O2 across 150 to 450 °C whereas molecular H2 cannot.
definition_note: at-H enables low-temperature reduction.
